Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so start with why my son has a zero on an essay he wrote himself.
Sit down, Hale. Owen found out about that zero from his phone in the middle of class. So you'll tell me why nobody called me first.
We're not here about the weather. Why was the zero entered before anyone called me?
"Hm." Is that your position? Because your school's procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered. Which part of that did you read differently?
